full_text_en:
Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch v. Shenzhen Airport Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan contract

Ruling Summary

1. According to the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Economic Dispute Cases Involving Suspected Economic Crimes, if an actor commits a crime by privately carving an official seal of a unit, or by using the unit's official seal, business introduction letter, or blank contract with the official seal affixed without authorization, as a method to conclude an economic contract, and the unit has obvious fault, and there is a causal relationship between such fault and the economic loss of the victim, the unit shall bear liability for compensation for the loss caused by such fault in accordance with law. The unit's defective internal rules and regulations, negligence in hiring personnel, and failure to effectively supervise its senior management personnel constitute specific manifestations of the unit having obvious fault.

2. Apparent agency refers to a situation where an actor, who has no authority to act, exceeds his authority, or continues to act as an agent after the termination of the agency, concludes a contract in the capacity of an agent, and the good faith counterparty objectively has sufficient reason to believe that the actor has authority to act. In such a case, the agency act is valid, and the principal shall bear civil liability to the counterparty in accordance with the contract. However, if the contract is used to conceal an illegal purpose under a lawful form, the contract is invalid under law, and in that case, the provisions of the Contract Law regarding apparent agency shall not apply.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2008) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 124

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Shenzhen Airport Co., Ltd., domiciled at 3rd and 4th Floors, No. 1 Office Building, Bao'an International Airport, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Huang Chuanqi, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Lu Chao, lawyer of Guangdong Guanghe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Hui, lawyer of Guangdong Renren Law Firm.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch, domiciled at 16th Floor, Jin'an Building, No. 300 Dongfeng Zhonglu, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Responsible Person: Zhang Changgong, President of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Zou Yuanchang, lawyer of Guangdong Dongfang Kunlun Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Haotian, lawyer of Beijing Jinge Law Firm.

The appellants, Shenzhen Airport Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenzhen Airport Company) and Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch (hereinafter referred to as Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch), appealed to this Court against the Civil Judgment (2005) Yue Gao Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 1 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court in a dispute over a loan contract. This Court lawfully constituted a collegial panel composed of presiding judge Zhang Shuming, acting judges Sha Ling and Zhou Lunjun to hear the case. Court clerk Zhao Suijun served as record-keeper. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts:

In October 2002, Cui Shaoxian (then General Manager of Shenzhen Airport Company, member of the Board of Directors, and in charge of the company's daily operations), using the official seal of Shenzhen Airport Company and in the name of Shenzhen Airport Company, entered into a bank acceptance contract with China Minsheng Bank, Guangzhou Branch for RMB 130 million. The RMB 130 million loaned out was transferred to Northwest Ya'ao Information Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Northwest Ya'ao Company), whose chairman was Zhang Yuming. Northwest Ya'ao Company issued a draft which was discounted at the Agricultural Bank of China, Yueyang Branch in Hunan. In March 2003, Cui Shaoxian, using the official seal of Shenzhen Airport Company and in the name of Shenzhen Airport Company, entered into a contract with Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, Guangzhou Branch (hereinafter referred to as SPD Bank Guangzhou Branch) for a loan of RMB 160 million. The RMB 160 million loan was used to repay the principal and interest on the previous loan from China Minsheng Bank, Guangzhou Branch. When this loan was about to mature, Cui Shaoxian personally discussed a loan with personnel from Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch, and introduced to the Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch personnel Li Zhenhai, a cashier of Northwest Ya'ao Company, as the assistant accountant of Shenzhen Airport Company. Cui instructed Li Zhenhai to impersonate a staff member of Shenzhen Airport Company (Cui personally altered his own business card and had new cards printed for Li Zhenhai), and using a privately carved official seal of Shenzhen Airport Company, on July 11, 2003, they entered into the Basic Credit Facility Contract with Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch. The contract stipulated that Industrial Bank would provide Shenzhen Airport Company with a basic credit facility with a maximum limit of RMB 300 million, to be used for resolving the normal working capital needs of Shenzhen Airport Company. The credit facility was valid from July 11, 2003 to July 10, 2004. On July 14 and December 9 of the same year, Li Zhenhai, acting on Cui Shaoxian's instructions and representing Shenzhen Airport Company in Cui Shaoxian's office, signed two loan contracts with Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch, one for RMB 200 million and the other for RMB 25 million, for a total loan amount of RMB 225 million, with an annual interest rate of 4.779% and a loan term of one year. All the documents required for opening the account and obtaining the loan, including the business license of Shenzhen Airport Company, tax registration certificate, legal representative identity certificate, power of attorney, board resolution, etc., were submitted by Cui Shaoxian and were affixed with the privately carved official seal of Shenzhen Airport Company. After the RMB 225 million loan was disbursed, Li Zhenhai, acting on Cui Shaoxian's instructions, transferred RMB 160 million of it through the account of Shenzhen Airport Air Cargo Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenzhen Airport Air Cargo Company) to repay the RMB 160 million loan from SPD Bank Guangzhou Branch, and the remaining funds were transferred to Northwest Ya'ao Company and other entities. When the RMB 225 million loan was about to mature, on July 5, 2004, Cui Shaoxian again personally used the forged official seal of Shenzhen Airport Company in his office to sign three loan contracts with Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch, each for RMB 75 million, to use new loans to repay the old loans, at an annual interest rate of 5.841% and a loan term of one year, thereby extending the repayment period for the RMB 225 million loan. On August 11, 2004, and January 4, 2005, Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch directly or through Ernst & Young sent loan confirmation letters and direct demand letters to Shenzhen Airport Company. Cui Shaoxian personally drafted reply letters, signed them, and used the forged official seal of Shenzhen Airport Company to respond to Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch.

After Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch disbursed the RMB 225 million loan, it received a total of RMB 6.67 million in loan interest up to November 24, 2004. Among this amount, Shenzhen Airport Air Cargo Company transferred in RMB 3.09 million; Shenzhen Shengtang Water Supply Equipment Industry Co., Ltd. transferred in RMB 0.9 million; Xinbao Industrial Development (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. transferred in RMB 0.1 million; Li Zhenhai paid RMB 1.88 million in cash; and RMB 0.7 million was transferred from Zhang Yuming's Shenzhen account.

The court of first instance also found: On February 24, 2005, Zhang Yuming, Cui Shaoxian, Li Zhenhai, and others were arrested by the Shenzhen Public Security Bureau on suspicion of loan fraud. On February 27, 2006, the Shenzhen People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution against Cui Shaoxian and others for suspected crimes before the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court. On August 7, 2007, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court rendered Criminal Judgment (2006) Shen Zhong Fa Xing Er Chu Zi No. 134 in the case concerning loan fraud by Cui Shaoxian, Zhang Yuming, Li Zhenhai, and others. The criminal judgment found the following facts: In May 2003, defendant Cui Shaoxian, in order to help defendant Zhang Yuming obtain financing, signed a basic credit facility contract for RMB 200 million and a loan contract for RMB 160 million with SPD Bank Guangzhou Branch in the name of Shenzhen Airport Company. The loan was taken over by Zhang Yuming's company. To repay the maturing loan, defendants Zhang Yuming and Cui Shaoxian decided to fraudulently use the name of Shenzhen Airport Company, under the pretext that funds were needed for the airport terminal expansion project, to obtain a loan from Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch. Defendants Zhang Yuming and Cui Shaoxian instructed defendant Li Zhenhai to impersonate a financial officer of Shenzhen Airport Company and handle the specific matters of obtaining the loan from Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch. On July 11 of the same year, defendant Li Zhenhai, impersonating a financial officer of Shenzhen Airport Company, signed a basic credit facility contract for RMB 300 million with Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch on behalf of the company. He forged the authorization letter of the legal representative of Shenzhen Airport Company, signed loan contracts for RMB 200 million and RMB 25 million respectively with Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch on behalf of the company, and affixed a forged official seal of Shenzhen Airport Company on the contracts and all loan documents. After the RMB 225 million was disbursed, all of it was transferred by Li Zhenhai to companies controlled by Zhang Yuming and was illegally possessed. In early 2004, when the RMB 225 million was about to mature, defendants Zhang Yuming, Cui Shaoxian, and Li Zhenhai adopted a method of borrowing new loans to repay old loans, using the remaining RMB 75 million credit line under the above credit facility contract to make three revolving loans, totaling RMB 225 million, thereby extending the repayment period by one year in a disguised form. Defendant Cui Shaoxian signed the loan extension contracts. Defendant Li Zhenhai affixed the forged official seal of Shenzhen Airport Company on the loan extension contracts. The judgment held that Zhang Yuming, Tian Qiwei, Cui Shaoxian, and Li Zhenhai, with the intent of illegal possession, used false supporting documents and economic contracts to defraud bank loans, and the amounts were especially huge, thus their actions constituted the crime of loan fraud. Zhang Yuming and Tian Qiwei constituted the crime of contract fraud. In the joint crimes, Zhang Yuming was the principal offender in both loan fraud and contract fraud. Tian Qiwei was an accessory in the loan fraud and a principal offender in the contract fraud. Although Cui Shaoxian did not possess the stolen proceeds in the loan fraud, he assisted Zhang Yuming in the loan fraud, helping Zhang Yuming illegally possess others' property, and thus was an accessory in the joint loan fraud crime. Given that Cui Shaoxian did not actually possess others' property, voluntarily surrendered after the crime and truthfully confessed his crime, which should be considered voluntary surrender; and after being apprehended, he assisted the public security authorities in arresting his co-defendants Zhang Yuming and Li Zhenhai, which constitutes a major meritorious act. Therefore, his punishment should be mitigated according to law. The court ruled: 1. Defendant Zhang Yuming was convicted of loan fraud and sentenced to life imprisonment, deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property; convicted of contract fraud and sentenced to life imprisonment, deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property. The combined sentence was life imprisonment, deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property. Defendant Tian Qiwei was convicted of loan fraud and sentenced to eight years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 10,000; convicted of contract fraud and sentenced to fifteen years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 20,000. The combined sentence was seventeen years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 30,000. Defendant Li Zhenhai was convicted of loan fraud and sentenced to fifteen years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 20,000. Defendant Cui Shaoxian was convicted of loan fraud and sentenced to six years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 10,000. 2. The seized forged seals were ordered to be confiscated and destroyed by the public security authorities. The proceeds of crime were ordered to be further recovered. After the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court rendered the first-instance criminal judgment, Zhang Yuming, Tian Qiwei, and Li Zhenhai appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court. Cui Shaoxian pleaded guilty at first instance and did not appeal after the judgment.

On January 2005, Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch filed an action with the court of first instance, requesting: 1. An order to rescind the Basic Credit Facility Contract signed on July 11, 2003, and the two loan contracts (for RMB 200 million and RMB 25 million respectively) signed based on that contract, as well as the three loan extension contracts (each for RMB 75 million) signed with Shenzhen Airport Company in July 2004 in the form of using new loans to repay old loans. 2. An order that Shenzhen Airport Company immediately return the loan principal of RMB 225 million, interest, and penalty interest of RMB 2,125,929.36 (total: RMB 227,125,929.36, calculated as of January 24, 2005). 3. An order that Shenzhen Airport Company bear all expenses incurred by Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch in realizing its creditor rights in this case. After the court of first instance accepted the case, because the Shenzhen Public Security Bureau was conducting a criminal investigation into the alleged loan fraud by former General Manager Cui Shaoxian and others of Shenzhen Airport Company, upon the application of Shenzhen Airport Company, the court ordered a stay of the trial on December 19, 2005. After the Shenzhen People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution before the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court against Cui Shaoxian and others for allegedly using contracts to defraud loans, and after the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court held a trial in the criminal case, the court of first instance resumed the trial.

The court of first instance held that the loans in this case were obtained through fraud by Cui Shaoxian and others, who, by carving a private official seal, signed loan contracts with Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch in the name of Shenzhen Airport Company. The Basic Credit Facility Contract and the loan contracts involved in this case all fall under the category of "using a lawful form to conceal an illegal purpose" as stipulated in Article 52(3) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and are contracts that violate prohibitive provisions of the law. Therefore, they should all be deemed invalid. The fraudulent loan conduct of Cui Shaoxian and others in the name of Shenzhen Airport Company has caused Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch to suffer losses of RMB 225 million in loans and related interest. The conduct of Cui Shaoxian and others in defrauding loans and the civil compensation relationship arising from the Basic Credit Facility Contract and the loan contracts involved in this case are two different types of legal relationships that are respectively governed by criminal law and civil law. Whether Shenzhen Airport Company should be liable for the losses of RMB 225 million in loans and related interest suffered by Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch due to the fraudulent loan conduct of Cui Shaoxian and others should be determined based on whether Shenzhen Airport Company had an obvious fault in relation to Cui Shaoxian's conduct and whether there is a causal relationship between such fault and the loan losses of Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch.

Cui Shaoxian was the General Manager and a director of the Board of Directors of Shenzhen Airport Company, and at that time was in charge of the company's daily operations. Cui Shaoxian, taking advantage of his position as General Manager, personally discussed loan matters with personnel from Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch, provided false identity (business cards, introduction letters, etc.) for Li Zhenhai, who signed the credit facility and loan contracts, provided a series of false documents for the fraud scheme, instructed Li Zhenhai to represent Shenzhen Airport Company using a forged official seal to sign loan contracts with Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch to obtain the loans by fraud, personally signed the two loan extension contracts, and signed confirmation letters in response to Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch's inquiries. Moreover, the two loan contracts involved in this case were signed in Cui Shaoxian's office. The above series of actions by Cui Shaoxian caused Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch to have reason to believe that Cui Shaoxian was acting in the course of his duties. The fact that Cui Shaoxian repeatedly used the name of Shenzhen Airport Company to fraudulently obtain huge loans over a period of more than two years without the knowledge of Shenzhen Airport Company indicates that the Board of Directors of Shenzhen Airport Company committed serious dereliction of duty, bearing a significant fault for failing to supervise and for being negligent in monitoring the company's senior management personnel. Moreover, this significant fault of the Board of Directors of Shenzhen Airport Company has a direct causal relationship with the loan losses of Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch. Therefore, Shenzhen Airport Company shall bear civil liability commensurate with its fault for the loan losses of Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch. Cui Shaoxian, using his position, used the genuine official seal of Shenzhen Airport Company to sign loan contracts with China Minsheng Bank and SPD Bank successively, fraudulently obtaining huge loans. Although the loans were not actually used by Shenzhen Airport Company, the liability for repayment to China Minsheng Bank and SPD Bank should, pursuant to law, be borne by Shenzhen Airport Company. Among the RMB 225 million loan involved in this case, RMB 160 million was used to repay the debt owed by Shenzhen Airport Company to SPD Bank. Therefore, Shenzhen Airport Company shall compensate Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch for this RMB 160 million.

As a commercial bank, Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch should have known that Shenzhen Airport Company is a listed company and that the requirements for granting loans to it are stricter than those for ordinary companies. However, when personnel from Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch negotiated the huge loans involved in this case, they only met and discussed with Cui Shaoxian, the General Manager of Shenzhen Airport Company, and Li Zhenhai. They failed to conduct strict examination in accordance with loan regulations of the authority of these two persons and the purpose and use of the loans. They failed to fulfill the duty of prudent care required of financial institutions when granting loans, and they lightly believed that Cui Shaoxian's actions were performed in the course of his duties, thereby enabling Cui Shaoxian, Li Zhenhai, and others to easily defraud the loans. Therefore, Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch also bears a significant fault for the losses caused by the fraudulent loans involved in this case and should share the loan losses in this case. For the total loss of RMB 225 million in loan principal and unpaid interest, apart from the RMB 160 million in principal and interest that Shenzhen Airport Company should compensate as stated above, the remaining loss of principal and interest of RMB 65 million shall be borne 50% by Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch itself, i.e., a loss of RMB 32.5 million in principal and interest. Compensation for the remaining loss of RMB 32.5 million in principal and interest shall still be borne by Shenzhen Airport Company. With respect to Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch's claim for expenses incurred in realizing its creditor rights, because there is no evidence to support it, that claim is not upheld.

After deliberation by its judicial committee, the court of first instance, pursuant to Article 52(3) and Article 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 35(1) of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China, Paragraph 2 of Article 5 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Economic Dispute Cases Involving Suspected Economic Crimes, and Article 138 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment: 1. Confirmed that the credit facility contract and the loan contracts involved in this case are all void. 2. Shenzhen Airport Company shall, within 15 days from the effective date of the judgment, compensate Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch for loan losses of RMB 192.5 million in principal and interest (interest calculated from November 25, 2004, at the benchmark lending rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period until the date of payment; for overdue payment, interest shall be calculated at double the benchmark lending rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period). 3. Rejected the other claims of Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch. The court acceptance fee for first instance was RMB 1,145,640, and the appraisal fee was RMB 480,000, totaling RMB 1,625,640. Shenzhen Airport Company shall bear RMB 1,137,948, and Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch shall bear RMB 487,692.

Both Shenzhen Airport Company and Industrial Bank Guangzhou Branch disagreed with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance and appealed to this Court.

Shenzhen Airport Company appealed, arguing: First, Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Disputes Involving Criminal Suspects" provides: "If an actor steals or embezzles the official seal, business letter of introduction, or blank contract form bearing the official seal of a unit, or privately engraves the official seal of a unit to enter into an economic contract, defrauding property for personal possession, use, disposition, or for other criminal activities, and if a crime is constituted, the unit shall not bear civil liability for the economic losses caused by the actor's criminal conduct." In this case, all loan materials were false, all official seals were forged, all bank accounts related to the loan were not genuine accounts of Shenzhen Airport Company, none of the funds were used by Shenzhen Airport Company, and the company's board of directors was completely unaware of the loan contracts and fund flows signed by Cui Shaoxian and others. Although Cui Shaoxian held the position of general manager, he did not have the authority to sign loan contracts of such a huge amount. According to the criminal judgment of the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court, he was an accomplice in the joint crime, playing a minor role in the fraud of RMB 225 million in loans. The loan fraud was entirely caused by the illegal and non-compliant conduct of the staff of Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch. There was no causal relationship between Cui Shaoxian's position as general manager and the economic losses of Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch. Shenzhen Airport Company had no fault in this case and should not bear compensation liability for the principal and interest of the loan in this case. Second, the original judgment found that Shenzhen Airport Company and Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch bore equal fault liability for the fraud of RMB 225 million in loans, and should have ruled that Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch bore 50% liability for all consequences after the fraud of RMB 225 million, not just 50% liability for RMB 65 million. During the trial of this case, the original court tried the loan dispute cases between China Minsheng Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch and Shenzhen Airport Company, and between Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch and Shenzhen Airport Company, which were not part of this case, finding that the RMB 225 million involved in this case was used to repay the loan owed by Shenzhen Airport Company to Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch. Therefore, Shenzhen Airport Company should compensate Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch for this RMB 160 million, and further ruled that the full RMB 160 million of the defrauded RMB 225 million involved in this case should be compensated by Shenzhen Airport Company. This violated the principle of "one lawsuit for one claim" in civil litigation and deprived Shenzhen Airport Company of the right to defend against the loan cases of China Minsheng Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch and Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch. Therefore, it requested the second instance to set aside item 2 of the original civil judgment and rule that Shenzhen Airport Company should not bear civil liability.

Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch appealed, arguing: Cui Shaoxian participated in the entire process of the RMB 225 million loan. Although Cui Shaoxian was not the legal representative of Shenzhen Airport Company, his identity was the managing director and general manager of Shenzhen Airport Company in charge of daily operations. All contracts in this case were signed in Cui Shaoxian's general manager's office within the premises of Shenzhen Airport Company. Although it was later confirmed that the official seals, board resolutions, and authorizations used by Cui Shaoxian in signing the contracts involved in the case in the name of Shenzhen Airport Company were forged, the formalities were complete at the time of signing. Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch had reason to believe that the actions of Cui Shaoxian and others constituted authorized agency and official conduct. Of the RMB 225 million loan in this case, RMB 160 million was used by Cui Shaoxian to repay a loan of RMB 160 million that should have been repaid by Shenzhen Airport Company to Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch. This shows that Shenzhen Airport Company was the actual user and beneficiary of the loan involved in the case. This loan transaction was a relationship between Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch and Shenzhen Airport Company, not a relationship with Cui Shaoxian personally. Although Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch failed to discover that the official seal and related documents provided by Cui Shaoxian were forged when signing the loan contract in this case, this negligence cannot be the basis for Shenzhen Airport Company to be exempted from all or part of its liability. Therefore, the conduct of Cui Shaoxian in signing the loan contract in this case with Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch in the name of Shenzhen Airport Company constituted apparent authority, and the contracts involved were all valid, having legal effect on the principal, Shenzhen Airport Company, which should repay all principal and interest (including penalty interest) of the loan in accordance with the contract. The facts found in the first-instance judgment were clear, but the result did not fully and comprehensively protect the legitimate rights and interests of Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch in accordance with the law. It requested the second instance to rule for the rescission of the basic credit contract involved in this case and the three short-term RMB loan contracts signed based on that contract totaling RMB 225 million; and to order Shenzhen Airport Company to repay the loan principal of RMB 225 million plus interest and penalty interest.

During the cross-examination at the second-instance hearing of this Court, neither Shenzhen Airport Company nor Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch submitted new evidence in this case, and both parties had no objection to the main facts found by the original court. Therefore, this Court affirms the facts found in the original judgment.

After the second-instance hearing, on December 8, 2008, this Court received a letter from Shenzhen Airport Company, stating that the criminal cases of Zhang Yuming, Tian Qiwei, and Li Zhenhai had been remanded for retrial by the Guangdong High People's Court, and requested that this case be remanded to the original court for retrial. In this regard, this Court holds that Shenzhen Airport Company has no objection to the main facts of this case, this case can be tried separately from the related criminal cases, and there is no reason for remand. Therefore, Shenzhen Airport Company's request is not supported.

Opinion of the Court: The focus of the second-instance issues is: the validity of the basic credit contract and related loan contracts signed between Shenzhen Airport Company and Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch; whether Cui Shaoxian's conduct constituted apparent authority; and the issue of civil liability of Shenzhen Airport Company and Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch.

According to the facts found in this case, the loans involved in this case were defrauded by Cui Shaoxian and others who forged documents, fabricated the purpose of the loan, and signed loan contracts with Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch in the name of Shenzhen Airport Company using a privately engraved official seal. The defrauded funds were all illegally possessed by companies controlled by Zhang Yuming, and Zhang Yuming, Cui Shaoxian, and Li Zhenhai are undergoing criminal investigation by the state judicial authorities. The true purpose of Cui Shaoxian and others was to defraud bank credit assets, and signing the basic credit contract and related loan contracts involved in this case was just a form and means to defraud bank credit assets. The above conduct falls under the circumstances of contract invalidity as provided in Article 52, item (3) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. The original judgment's finding that the basic credit contract and related loan contracts involved in this case were concluded for an illegal purpose in the form of a legal act, and thus invalid, is not improper, and this Court affirms it.

This Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Disputes Involving Criminal Suspects" provides: "If an actor, by privately engraving or without authorization using the official seal, business letter of introduction, or blank contract form bearing the official seal of a unit, commits a crime through entering into an economic contract, and if the unit has clear fault and there is a causal relationship between that fault and the victim's economic losses, the unit shall, in accordance with the law, bear compensation liability for the losses caused by that fault." Cui Shaoxian was a director and general manager of Shenzhen Airport Company, in charge of the company's daily operations during the period of this case. To repay overdue loans from other commercial banks, Cui Shaoxian, together with Zhang Yuming, Li Zhenhai, and others, personally discussed loan matters with staff of Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch, provided false documents and forged board resolutions, instructed Li Zhenhai to represent Shenzhen Airport Company in signing the credit contract and loan contracts using a privately engraved official seal, and subsequently personally used the privately engraved official seal to sign a new loan contract with Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch to replace the old loan, causing Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch to mistakenly believe that Cui Shaoxian was acting in the scope of his duties and that the loans were made by Shenzhen Airport Company, thus ultimately succeeding in defrauding RMB 225 million. The occurrence of the above situation was mainly due to Cui Shaoxian's use of his special status to participate in the fraud activity, but it was also inseparable from Shenzhen Airport Company's unsound rules and regulations, negligence in personnel selection, and inadequate supervision of senior management personnel. Therefore, Shenzhen Airport Company had clear fault in this case and shall, in accordance with the law, bear primary compensation liability for the losses of Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch.

During the process of signing and performing the RMB 225 million loan contract in this case, Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch failed to exercise prudent attention, did not conduct necessary identification and verification of the privately engraved official seal of Shenzhen Airport Company, the forged supporting documents, and the board resolutions, and had obvious omissions in the stages of loan review, disbursement, and post-lending tracking inspection. Shenzhen Airport Company, as a listed company, did not disclose the loans involved in this case in its semi-annual and annual reports for a period of up to two years. Industrial Bank also failed to detect this and take corresponding measures, instead signing a new contract to replace the old loan with it. Therefore, Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch also had some fault in this case and should bear corresponding civil liability for the losses in this case.

Regarding the appeal of Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch that Cui Shaoxian's conduct in this case constituted apparent authority, that the credit contract and related series of loan contracts in this case were valid, and that Shenzhen Airport Company should repay the loan principal and interest (including penalty interest) in accordance with the loan contracts. This Court holds: Apparent authority is when an actor, without authority, exceeds authority, or continues to act as an agent after authority has terminated, enters into a contract in the name of the principal, and the bona fide counterpart objectively has sufficient reason to believe that the actor has authority. In such cases, the agency act is valid, and the principal shall bear civil liability with the counterpart in accordance with the contract. However, when the counterpart is at fault, whether intentional or negligent, there is no room for the application of apparent authority. Since the basic credit contract and related loan contracts in this case were invalid contracts concealing illegal purposes in a legal form, and Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch was at fault in the loan process of this case, the provisions of the Contract Law on apparent authority do not apply to this case. Shenzhen Airport Company and Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch shall bear corresponding civil liability according to their respective degrees of fault.

Regarding the civil liability of the parties in this case, the original court determined that RMB 160 million of the RMB 225 million was a previous debt that Shenzhen Airport Company should repay to Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch, and that Shenzhen Airport Company should bear full responsibility for that portion of the loss, while the remaining RMB 65 million should be borne 50% each by Shenzhen Airport Company and Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch. In this regard, this Court holds: The original judgment's determination of the loss amount and the principle for apportioning civil liability in this case was erroneous, and it was improper to order Shenzhen Airport Company to bear full repayment responsibility for the previous debt of RMB 160 million. This should be corrected. Of the RMB 225 million, RMB 160 million was indeed used by Cui Shaoxian and others to repay the previous debt owed to Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch. However, whether Shenzhen Airport Company should repay the RMB 160 million loan to Shanghai Pudong Development Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch is irrelevant to this case. That repayment did not change the nature of the RMB 225 million fraud. In this case, the loss should be determined as RMB 225 million plus unpaid interest, which should define the scope of civil liability. Nevertheless, although the original judgment's determination of the loss amount and the proportion of civil liability apportionment was not entirely appropriate, the judgment's order that Shenzhen Airport Company compensate Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch for a principal loss of RMB 192.5 million plus unpaid interest, and that Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch bear a principal loss of RMB 32.5 million plus interest by itself, i.e., Shenzhen Airport Company bearing nearly 85% of the principal and interest loss on the RMB 225 million loan in this case, and Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch bearing nearly 15% of the principal and interest loss by itself, the liability of the parties is commensurate with their degree of fault. Therefore, the amounts of loss borne by the parties as determined in the original judgment are not improper, and this Court affirms this.

In summary, the original judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. Although the determination of the loss amount and the proportion of liability apportionment was not entirely appropriate, the result was not improper. The appeal requests of Shenzhen Airport Company and Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch lack factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support them. In accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 1,177,429.65 is to be borne by Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Branch in the amount of RMB 588,714.825, and by Shenzhen Airport Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 588,714.825.

This judgment is final.
